cause.note: review desk round 1 — independent Codex reviewer, seven findings above the severity line, all accepted

changes.what: Authority-bearing values (principal, grant, revocation, authorization) now carry a Provenance established from the authenticated record outside the bytes; their decoders take it as a required input and cross-check every identity-bearing field against it. Authorization gains a required explicit-yes record; a grant's grantor carries its source reference.
changes.why: A faulty adapter could promote content-supplied fields while satisfying every listed shape; nothing bound the value to the record that produced it.

changes.what: Result and Outcome now claim only recognition at compile time; behaviour (a refusal reported as success, a budget applied treated as an error, an uncertain outcome retried) is held by one consumption function plus an architecture lint. Fixtures NF-14, NF-15, NF-46 moved from compile to lint.
changes.why: A tagged union cannot stop a caller from matching a variant and then misbehaving; the guarantee was overstated.

changes.what: The protected-artifact answer is narrowed to repository merges, where the host's branch rules are the external anchor; dashboard-governed and runtime artifacts are declared an open question carried to parts nine and eleven, and the circular 'decoder on its own protected list' claim is removed.
changes.why: Branch protection does not protect artifacts the agent can edit with filesystem authority, and a decoder cannot enforce the list that protects it.

changes.what: Equality is declared three ways (identity, version, value) and each type section names which it supports; same identity with incompatible immutable fields yields a Conflict value, never equality or silent latest-wins.
changes.why: No type actually declared its equality, and identity equality hid the cross-machine conflicts the big picture requires to be recorded.

changes.what: Seventeen negative fixtures added (NF-54 to NF-70) so every named rejection has a stable fixture, and the coverage claim is restated as a build step mapping table cells to fixtures.
changes.why: The claim that every table row was a numbered fixture was false.

changes.what: Rule citations corrected: 100 removed from canonical bytes and authorization; 64 and 75 removed from measurement; 107 and 111 removed from evidence (the weakest-strength aggregate is now a marked Value); 101 and 103 removed from the authorization and requester-authorizer rules; 93 removed from standing grants.
changes.why: Each cited a rule that does not govern the claim.

changes.what: An explicit inventory table lists every constitutional value (eleven core, seven supporting, including Revocation, Provenance, Conflict, UnresolvedInput) with its constructor, and the completeness checks range over it.
changes.why: The prose count of nine types was not stable, so complete schema registration and fixture coverage were uncheckable.

cause.note: first version: the constitutional types and the decoding boundary, the first part design the approved big picture names

changes.why: The big-picture design (section 13) orders the part designs and puts constitutional types and runtime decoders first; the register (kind 12) hands the protected-artifact enforcement question to this step.
